partners.mechanism_chain: DYSF (HGNC:2798) —DISRUPTS→ sarcomere integrity (GO:0030050); sarcomere integrity (GO:0030050) —LEADS_TO→ Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (HP:0003688); MYH11 (HGNC:7639) —DISRUPTS→ myosin filament assembly (GO:0031440); myosin filament assembly (GO:0031440) —DISRUPTS→ sarcomere organization (GO:0045205); sarcomere organization (GO:0045205) —LEADS_TO→ Visceral myopathy (HP:0011701); sarcomere integrity (GO:0030050) —BINDS→ sarcomere organization (GO:0045205); myosin filament assembly (GO:0031440) —BINDS→ sarcomere organization (GO:0045205). Loss-of-function mutations in DYSF (LGMD2B) and MYH11 (visceral myopathy 2) converge on the disruption of sarcomere organization and function. DYSF is involved in sarcolemma repair, and its dysfunction can indirectly impair sarcomere integrity. MYH11 is a component of the smooth muscle myosin filament, and its dysfunction directly impairs myosin filament assembly and thus sarcomere organization in visceral smooth muscle. Both pathways converge on the general pathway of sarcomere organization, affecting muscle contractility and leading to distinct but related muscular dystrophies.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that pathogenic variants in DYSF and MYL11 do not impact the core machinery or efficiency of the ubiquitin-proteasome system, or that the affected downstream cellular processes are entirely distinct and unlinked. _(variant: None specified for these rare diseases, but a common variant in DYSF or MYL11 with a frequency >0.01 in gnomAD would weaken the claim of pathogenicity.)_
